title: Release tranche prioritization and communication pathways for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Coordinate tranche-based cut criteria, release notes ownership and cross-team comms for the March release covering API, Console and Runtime. Goal: define slicing of work into 3 tranches (critical hot fixes + GA features + deferred low-risk improvements), prescribe gating signals per tranche, and align release notes and GTM comms so customers have clear migration and rollback guidance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tranche definitions and gating matrix finalized and signed off by Eng/Design/Sales/Docs. 2) Release notes template populated and owners assigned for every notable change. 3) Cut criteria automation hooks (dashboard alerts + PR label checklist) in place before scope freeze. 4) Internal comms schedule and escalation path documented.
comments: 2025-02-12 Asha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after cross-functional readout. Proposed tranche split: T1 (safety/bugfixes), T2 (GA features), T3 (nice-to-have). Asked Eng to propose measurable metrics for gating.

2025-02-14 Miguel Santos: Eng response - suggested gating signals: P0 defects cleared, 90th pct token latency < 220ms on canary, error rate < 0.2% across top 10 routes. Will prototype automated checks in CI for PR labeling.

2025-02-16 Design (Lina Park): Design review - Console rollout UI notes need a screenshot diffs checklist; propose adding a 'visual-verify' owner for each Console change. Marking as dependency for design QA.
2025-02-17 Docs (Ravi Patel): Release notes template draft uploaded. Requesting owners list for each bullet by 2025-02-21 so we can prepare user-facing messaging and migration steps.
2025-02-18 Sales Ops (Marta Ruiz): GTM comms - recommend two customer segments: early adopters on Dedicated, and regulated customers on Private. Need separate playbooks for each tranche.
2025-02-19 Miguel Santos: Added automation plan - PR label 'release:T1/T2/T3' enforced by CI lint; dashboard alert mapping in Grafana created; will open ENG ticket to implement checks (ENG-24102).

2025-02-20 Asha Kapoor: PM review - consolidated gating matrix at Confluence link and scheduled tranche signoff meeting for 2025-02-24. Assigned docs and comm owners; pending engineering metric verification.
decisions: Adopt 3-tranche model to reduce scope flip risk and provide predictable rollback windows.

Gating thresholds: T1 requires zero P0 open defects and security signoff; T2 requires 90th pct latency < 220ms and <0.2% error rate on canary; T3 is feature-flagged and allowed with higher leniency subject to evals.
Release notes will be owned at feature level by PMs with a central Docs owner responsible for editorial and GTM packaging.
Console visual checks will be handled by design owners with a 'visual-verify' tag on PRs; automated screenshot comparisons optional for high-risk UI surfaces.
risks: Late discovery of perf regression in runtime impacting T2 timing.
Insufficient owner assignment for release notes resulting in last-minute copy gaps.
Confusion across Customer Success / Sales about which tranche applies to a given account tier.
Automation for PR labels might not be complete before scope freeze, causing manual triage overhead.
mitigations: Run a pre-freeze synthetic load test window (2025-02-28 to 2025-03-01) and require signoff from reliability lead.
Docs runbook: assign 'owner' field per bullet and escalate unassigned items 48 hours before freeze.
Sales playbook: create tranche-to-customer-mapping table and host 30-minute sync with CS leads.
Manual fallback: triage rota for PR labeling during the first 72 hours post-freeze.
next_steps: 2025-02-21: Engineering to provide concrete metric sources and automate the Grafana alerts (owner: Miguel).
2025-02-21: PMs submit feature-to-tranche mapping spreadsheet (owner: Asha).
2025-02-22: Docs to publish release notes template and request owners (owner: Ravi).
2025-02-24: Tranche signoff meeting with Eng/Design/Docs/Sales/CS scheduled (organizer: Asha).
2025-02-28: Pre-freeze synthetic load window and canary run (owner: Reliability).
notes: Prefer soft scope locks per component (Console vs Runtime) to allow emergency T1 patches without blocking UI improvements in T3.
We will track cut decisions in a single artifacts page to avoid multiple conflicting spreadsheets.
Consider a 'rolling notes' approach in Drive where PRs append their note bullet to reduce merge conflicts in the release notes doc.
